transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-06 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Lina Park, Marcus Holt (Redwood); Priya Menon, Ethan Zhao, Rita Alvarez, Jamal Beck (Cobalt)

Summary: quick sync to align legal and procurement on acceptance criteria. Some back-and-forth on DPA timings, SSO, and pilot pricing.

[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Lina from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. Marcus and i will walk through the acceptance ask and next steps.
[00:12] Priya Menon: Thanks Lina, Priya here, quick note we only have 30ish minutes for commercial today, legal joined for the redline bits.
[00:20] Marcus Holt: Hi, Marcus - i'll be the technical point. we'll keep it tight, and then set the security deep dive after.
[00:32] Jamal Beck: Jamal from legal, we've seen the MSA draft, a few DPA items flagged - mainly subprocessor notice windows and deletion timing.
[00:45] Lina Park: Yep understood. our standard DPA has 30 days for subprocessor notice, but we can propose a 14-day carve for enterprise. that was something we wanted to discuss.
[00:58] Rita Alvarez: On deletion, we need assurance on the private deployment and egress path for PII. we also want KMS integration so keys are customer-managed.
[01:12] Marcus Holt: For Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. note there are two options for onboarding: VPC peering or private link style - both support BYOK but the cert rotation cadence differs slightly.
[01:30] Ethan Zhao: Can you lay out where audit logs live? we need at least a 13 month retention and immutable trails for regulatory audits.
[01:43] Marcus Holt: Audit logs are available via our console and can be forwarded to your SIEM through S3 or syslog. retention settings are configurable; we can also arrange a longer retention export if needed.
[01:57] Lina Park: quick commercial note - for pilot we typically do a committed reserved bucket for 3 months to allow reliable latency SLOs. pricing sketches are in the doc i sent but we can convert to a pilot quote once we get volumes.
[02:17] Priya Menon: Procurement wants a pricing ladder and approval route - can you show the approval timelines?
[02:27] Lina Park: Sure - typical flow: pilot quote -> procurement approval -> legal MSA sign -> production commit. we aim to have procurement and legal sign within 2-3 weeks for an expedited intake; otherwise it's 6-8 weeks.
[02:42] Jamal Beck: On the MSA, we will need explicit SLA metrics and credits table included. can you propose SLO targets?
[02:52] Marcus Holt: For hosted LLM endpoints our standard is 99.5% monthly availability for generation endpoints with p99.9 latency under small load; dedicated pools can be 99.9% with contractual credits. For mission-critical finance workloads we recommend Dedicated with reserved concurrency.
[03:11] Rita Alvarez: What's your definition of availability? do cache hit rate issues count?
[03:18] Marcus Holt: Availability is measured at the model route level — errors and full route unavailability; degradation due to external infra (customer VPC) is scoped out. prefix/KV cache is considered internal optimization and wouldn't count toward downtime unless it causes actual errors.
[03:36] Priya Menon: We also need data residency control - storage in EU for EU customers. Is that selectable for the Private deployment?
[03:45] Lina Park: Yes, with Private we can pin regionally; hosted customers can choose region for storage but private gives full control.
[03:54] Jamal Beck: About indemnities and export controls - we've seen a special clause from security that requires export compliance language, can Redwood accept that?
[04:03] Lina Park: We can scope export control carve-outs; i'll flag legal on typical redlines. for extreme cases we do an exec exception route.
[04:13] Marcus Holt: Technical aside - for high-context prompts we recommend quantized model variants and pre-warming the KV cache to keep tail-latency down, that affects compute and pricing.
[04:29] Ethan Zhao: Pricing - can you separate cost into baseline and tail-costs? we need a predictable baseline for budgeting, but also headroom for spikes.
[04:40] Lina Park: Absolutely. baseline reserved capacity + burst on usage. baseline covers standard token pricing and a lower per-token rate for reserved; spike usage billed at overage. we will send a worked example.
[04:55] Priya Menon: On approvals, finance needs a 1 pager that shows monthly forecast and worst-case egress fees.
[05:04] Lina Park: we'll include egress modeling. can you confirm expected monthly tokens and peak QPS? that will make the model concrete.
[05:12] Ethan Zhao: we can provide an initial estimate: 800M tokens/month, peak 300 QPS during batch windows, average 50 QPS. call it a placeholder.
[05:27] Marcus Holt: great, with 800M tokens we'll recommend Dedicated for economics, but we can pilot Hosted behind a gateway to validate accuracy and latency before a full Dedicated commit.
[05:40] Rita Alvarez: Security question: SSO - we need SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, RBAC that maps to our AD groups. can Redwood support that for both Hosted and Private?
[05:55] Marcus Holt: Yes SAML and SCIM are supported. RBAC mapping is available in the console; for Private we can sync directly to your AD via SCIM.
[06:07] Jamal Beck: Any concerns around subprocessor chains and vendor-of-vendor? we require a 14-day notice before new subprocessor onboarding.
[06:18] Lina Park: we can commit to 14-day notice for major subprocessors; for minor infra changes we may give notice in the portal and via regular security bulletins.
[06:33] Priya Menon: Also need encryption at rest and in transit - standard?
[06:37] Marcus Holt: Already standard: TLS 1.2+ for transit and AES-256 for rest; BYOK is supported for Private.
[06:46] Lina Park: quick timeline proposal: customer shares volumes by Mon 2026-08-09, Redwood sends redline + pilot quote by Tue 2026-08-10, security deep dive scheduled for week of Aug 11, pilot kickoff targeted Aug 18. does that work?
[06:59] Ethan Zhao: that timeline is tight but doable. procurement needs 48 hours to review pricing after we get the doc.
[07:09] Priya Menon: we'll prioritize. one more ask: we need a copy of SOC2 Type 2 and recent pen test summary before legal signs.
[07:18] Lina Park: yes we will provide SOC2 and the summary, plus an architecture diagram with egress paths.
[07:26] Jamal Beck: On SLAs, can you draft a credits table - say 99.9% uptime gives 10% credit, 99.5% gives 5% - standard bands?
[07:36] Lina Park: we have standard bands, but we can draft a custom credit schedule for enterprise. i'll include that with the MSA redline.
[07:45] Marcus Holt: technical note: to hit p99.9 under your peak we'd want pinned workers and CPU/GPU sizing; i'll include a sample pool size for expected QPS.
[07:57] Ethan Zhao: will you run a latency sim for our 2k-8k token prompts? that's critical for UX decisioning.
[08:05] Marcus Holt: yes, we'll run a short latency benchmark using your sample prompts. can you share a representative prompt set and dataset? obfuscate PII if needed.
[08:18] Priya Menon: we'll send samples to Marcus by Monday.
[08:25] Lina Park: perfect. a couple procedural notes: procurement would like a procurement-only copy of the pricing (no engineering details) that goes to finance. legal wants the full MSA redline. and security will get the pack.
[08:40] Priya Menon: understood. for billing path we need invoice cadence and audit rights - can you support quarterly invoicing and audit window?
[08:51] Lina Park: quarterly invoicing is fine. audit rights are standard with notice and reasonable scope; i'll have legal confirm the exact language.
[09:01] Jamal Beck: one negotiation point - data deletion: finance wants immediate suspension and deletion with certification within 30 days for test data, but for production datasets we asked for 60 day window. can Redwood accept staggered retention commitments?
[09:18] Marcus Holt: technically yes, we can handle tiered deletion policies per dataset tag. we'll surface how deletion requests are handled in the runbook.
[09:30] Priya Menon: ok good.
[09:35] Lina Park: to summarize next steps - we collect volumes and prompts, send redline + pilot quote, schedule security deep dive, run latency sims. are we aligned?
[09:47] Ethan Zhao: yes aligned.
[09:50] Rita Alvarez: quick follow: for the deep dive can you include network engineers so we can confirm VPC routing and egress encryption?
[09:58] Marcus Holt: yes we'll have infra and network on that call.
[10:03] Priya Menon: procurement will expect pricing in a clean one-pager for approvals.
[10:09] Lina Park: will do. i'll circle back with timings after this call.
[10:15] Jamal Beck: I have a small question on liability caps, will Redwood negotiate a higher liability cap for financial services?
[10:23] Lina Park: We have standard tiers; for FS customers we often agree to a higher cap tied to usage commitments, we can flag that for legal.
[10:35] Ethan Zhao: one last tech ask - are you able to provide a read-only replica of model outputs into our environment for auditing?
[10:44] Marcus Holt: yes, we can stream model outputs to your S3 bucket or event stream for audit; need to sort throughput and retention.
[10:54] Priya Menon: thanks everyone, we'll look for the MSA redline and the pricing one-pager.
[11:00] Lina Park: thanks all, we'll follow up. End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: some words auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., "BYOK" as "BY-O-K" at times), speaker attribution was manually adjusted in places.

Attachments mentioned: redline draft (link: https://redwood.example.com/drafts/COB-MSA-redline), pilot pricing sketch (link: https://redwood.example.com/quotes/COB-pilot-0826), SOC2 summary (to be shared).
